🌍 Ghalibaf: Any threat against Iran will draw swift, regret-inducing response

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned that any threat or adventurism against the Islamic Republic will be met with a “swift and regret-inducing” response, saying the Iranian nation will not retreat in the face of threats, rhetoric, or economic and air blockades.

Addressing an open session of the Parliament on Tuesday, Ghalibaf said US leaders should understand that the Iranian people will not be intimidated by threats or pressure.
​
“The leaders of the White House should know that the great and history-making nation of Iran will never retreat in the face of saber-rattling and rhetoric or an air or trade blockade, and the response of the Islamic Republic of Iran to any threat or adventurism will be harshly regret-inducing and swift,” he said.
​
Ghalibaf said US attempts to impose a maritime blockade, close air corridors, and exert maximum pressure on Iran’s trade routes will fail through serious economic planning and military responses similar to those employed during Iraq’s war of aggression against Iran in the 1980s.
​
He said Iran’s history of resistance showed that the country should not be intimidated by siege and threats.
​
“If the enemy’s American decision-making apparatus fails to understand this fundamental truth, it will continue to be caught in the cycle of receiving heavy slaps from the Iranian nation,” he said.
​
Ghalibaf also criticized “light-headed” remarks by US President Donald Trump at the United Nations General Assembly, saying such hostile statements showed Washington has not changed its behavior toward Iran.
​
The parliament speaker further referred to Trump’s recent remarks concerning the Strait of Hormuz and the passage of ships through the strategic waterway.
​
“Both the US and other countries should know that, as we have said, in a region where we do not sell oil, no one will sell oil, and if our security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe,” he said.
​
Ghalibaf also praised President Masoud Pezeshkian’s address to the UN General Assembly, saying he spoke as the true representative of the Iranian people and a “proud and revolutionary nation” that will not bow to threats or domination.
​
He described a Monday message by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, as a precise formulation of a “defense and civilizational doctrine,” arguing that Iran’s deterrence structure has been built through previous wars and that recent wars demonstrated a change in the balance of threats.

🇦🇷🇬🇧 Argentina gives London two weeks to halt Falklands oil project

Argentine President Javier Milei has issued the UK a two-week ultimatum to stop work on the Sea Lion offshore oilfield near the disputed Falkland (Malvinas) Islands, a project run by Israel's Navitas Petroleum and Britain's Rockhopper Exploration.

If London does not comply by around 12 October, Buenos Aires says it will ask the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea in Hamburg to impose a temporary halt. Milei has also launched arbitration proceedings under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, calling the project the "plundering" of Argentine resources.

"Argentina will not sit idly by," his office said, accusing Britain of causing "irreversible and irreparable" damage.

The field is estimated to hold 1.7 billion barrels. An Argentine court already ordered work suspended this month pending an environmental review, and Buenos Aires argues the project violates UN resolutions barring unilateral action while the sovereignty dispute remains unresolved.

Britain has occupied the islands since 1833 and rejects Argentina's claim, citing a 2013 referendum in which residents voted to remain a British overseas territory.

🎙 Iranian, Nigerien FMs discuss expanding mutual ties

📌 Tehran, IRNA –Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Nigerien counterpart, Bakary Yaou Sangare, have met on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly, discussing bilateral relations and international developments.

Araghchi—who has traveled to New York to attend the annual UNGA sessions— sat down with Sangare on Monday evening, with the talks being largely focused on Iran-Niger ties, as well as issues of common concern.
​
The two top diplomats, while expressing satisfaction over growing bilateral relations, also discussed ways to boost them and foster joint cooperation within the framework of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).
​
Emphasizing Iran's determination to strengthen relations with African nations—especially AES members—the Foreign Minister expressed hope that a joint meeting between Iran and the three member states of the Sahel alliance would be held at the earliest.
​
Araghchi expressed gratitude for the solidarity shown by the people of Niger with the Iranian nation and government, in the face of illegal and unjustified military aggression launched by the United States and the Israeli regime.  He also commended Niger’s principled stance in opposing the instrumental use of the IAEA Board of Governors against Iran.
​
He further underscored Iran's support for the Nigerien government's efforts to safeguard its independence and national sovereignty, maintain security and stability, and advance its development programs.
​
During his stay in New York, Araghchi met and held discussions with dozens of his counterparts from various countries as well as representatives of international organizations, on the sidelines of this year's UN General Assembly.
